_comment-vendored: VENDORED into vibe3d (task 0616). Single-header image decoder, upstream nothings/stb @ 013ac3beddff3dbffafd5177e7972067cd2b5083 (stb_image.h v2.30), dual-licensed MIT / public domain (Unlicense) -- see LICENSE. stb_image.h is byte-identical to upstream; stb_image_impl.c is the local translation unit that instantiates the implementation, restricts the compiled format set, disables the stdio path, and sets the compile-time dimension cap -- see PATCHES.md. Built with CMake+Ninja, mirroring third_party/nfde's shape -- that prerequisite is already required by this build (nfde), and it sidesteps a real failure mode: routing a single-file C library through dub's own built-in C-source compilation (its ImportC front end) fails on this project's dev host because the system libc headers use a C23 `nullptr` construct ImportC does not parse -- CMake invokes the platform's actual C compiler instead.

_comment-prebuild: These commands must be INCREMENTAL. This package is a `sourceLibrary`, so it has no artifact of its own and dub can never judge it up to date -- its preBuildCommands therefore run on every build that builds anything at all. The linux/osx lines used to begin with `rm -rf $..._PACKAGE_DIR/out`, which threw the previous result away and recompiled the translation unit every time: measured on this host, the cold C compile is 2.46s against 0.00s for a warm re-run, and because `out/libstb_image_vendor.a` is also this package's `lflags` input, deleting it made the CONSUMING executable stale too -- so a `dub build` with nothing whatsoever changed still relinked vibe3d, 7.9s instead of the 0.2s dub spends deciding there is nothing to do. Re-running `cmake -B` over an existing build directory is the supported incremental path (a changed `-D...` on the command line overwrites the cached entry; a build directory that cannot be reused -- e.g. the package was moved -- makes CMake fail loudly rather than silently produce a stale library), and `cmake -B` creates the directory itself, which is why there is no `mkdir` either. The windows lines never had the wipe; all three platforms now agree.
